newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks seen higher barring Q4 GDP upset.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks seen higher barring Q4 GDP upset.

text.p: Wall Street stocks look set to open higher barring any upset in the fourth quarter real gross domestic product, due to be released at 0830 EST/1330 GMT.
"Right now, the futures are up and the opening looks okay," said Larry Wachtel, analyst at Prudential Securities. "But it all depends on the numbers."

He said that while the GDP was old news, covering as it did the previous quarter, a stronger than anticipated rise could still send bonds into a tailspin, with stocks streaming behind them into negative territory.
The GDP is expected to register an increase of 3.9 percent compared 2.1 percent in the previous quarter, according to a Reuter survey of U.S. economists.
The Price Index is expected to rise 2.2 percent compared with 2.0 percent in the third quarter while implicit deflator is seen up 1.8 percent compared with 1.7 percent.
"The GDP will tell us we had a strong quarter. But if it comes in above consenus, if it rise above four percent, the bond market will back off," Wachtel said.
He said that the market rally broadened out on Thursday and that the market's upward momentum was back.
"Bonds willing, we'll do better today," Wachtel said.
Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments, said the GDP was old news but with any real pick-up in inflation, the bond market would fall.

"The market is now approaching the higher end of the trading range, and even if the GDP news is positive we are due for a pullback. Maybe not today, but certainly next week," he said. The trading range was between 6400 and 6800, he said.
In Tokyo, the Nikkei Average leapt 465.97 points, or 2.61 percent, to close at 18,610.20.
In London, the FTSE 100 Index was up 25.8 at 4254.2.
Among U.S. shares traded in London, International Business Machines Corp was down 1/2 at 157-3/8, Intel Corp slipped 3/4 to 159-3/8 and Texas Instruments Inc fell 1/4 to 74-3/8.
The dollar crawled above 122 in Tokyo and was weaker in Europe, testing 1.63 marks.
U.S. Treasuries were mostly higher, with the long bond up 5/32 to yield 6.86 percent.

The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street writes that the stock of Santa Anita Realty Enterprises Inc has more than doubled in just over five months and the company is now officially up for sale following two abortive attempts to take it over at a much lower price.
The paper said that while some savvy fund managers have been enjoying the ride, others believe that the stock could be nearing its peak.
The New York Times Market Place writes that shares in Gilead Sciences Inc soared earlier this week after the company announced that it would soon begin clinical tests of a drug to treat influenza.
But a little known Australian company, Biota Holdings Ltd, has a similar drug well advanced in human trials and could beat Gilead to the market by at least two years, the New York Times said.
